cards.headline: The final stretch: Essential listening tips for PSLE pupils
bullets: The PSLE listening test is two weeks away.
Parents often drill kids with practice papers.
Experts say understanding mistakes helps more than just doing more practice.
Tips are available online to help children do better.

cards.headline: Free breakfast packs, AI study tool, stress-busting activities to support PSLE pupils
bullets: 12,000 Primary 6 students can get free breakfast bundles from Sept 3 to 6.
A new free resource called Rest Papers offers fun activities to help students relax.
Students can try a free trial of cher.ai, an AI tool for English revision practice.
The AI tool provides feedback on grammar, composition, and oral exams.

cards.headline: Shattered glass, water seepage: Canberra Residences owners sue contractor over unresolved defects
bullets: Canberra Residences owners are suing the contractor over unfinished repairs more than ten years after moving in.
Residents claim issues like water leaks, shattered balcony glass, and poor paintwork remain unresolved.
The lawsuit alleges the contractor breached a 2020 settlement agreement meant to fix these defects.
Problems first appeared soon after residents moved in, with over half experiencing water seepage.
Thousands of balcony glass panels have reportedly shattered since the condo was built.

cards.headline: How to do more parenting by doing less
bullets: Parents are spending more time, money, and energy on kids than ever before.
Some parents feel they must supervise kids closely and fill their schedules.
The article suggests parents can help kids by doing less for them.
It encourages creating moments for children to experience independence.

cards.headline: New online directory to provide one-stop shop of programmes for Malay/Muslim community
bullets: A new online directory called M³+ Directory lists programmes and services for the Malay/Muslim community.
The directory covers areas like financial help and job support.
It aims to make it easier for people to find the help they need.
The platform also helps organisations work together and find gaps in services.

cards.headline: About 1,200 BTO flats in Toa Payoh, Sin Ming to have shorter waiting time of under 3 years
bullets: About 1,200 new HDB flats in Toa Payoh and Sin Ming will have waiting times under three years.
These flats are part of efforts to build more homes and speed up waiting times for buyers.
Construction is expected to be well underway when buyers book their units.
New homes are also planned for Toa Payoh West and Mount Pleasant over the next decade.

cards.headline: Singapore architect Chang Yong Ter believes good architecture can make us better humans
bullets: Architect Chang Yong Ter believes good buildings can make people better.
His early Elok House project featured trees growing through its floors.
Chang designs homes inspired by nature, spirituality, and client needs.
He also runs a children's enrichment centre focused on nature and play.

cards.headline: More mosquitoes, less birdsong: Increasingly extreme El Ninos may favour pests while other animals swelter
bullets: More extreme El Nino weather could mean more mosquitoes in Singapore.
Dengue risk rises with stronger El Nino conditions, according to a study.
Cockroaches and pigeons may thrive as they adapt well to human environments.
Native animals like birds and langurs may struggle with heat and less rain.
Hotter weather can harm bird reproduction and reduce insect numbers.

cards.headline: Fire involving about 3ha of greenery extinguished near Seletar Link
bullets: Firefighters put out a large vegetation fire near Seletar Link on Saturday.
The blaze covered about 3 hectares, roughly four football fields.
No one was injured in the incident.
The cause of the fire is still being investigated.

cards.headline: No appeal from Bloomberg on Shanmugam, Tan See Leng defamation case
bullets: Bloomberg and its reporter will pay ministers S$230,000 each in damages.
Bloomberg and its reporter did not appeal the court's defamation ruling.
A court found a Bloomberg article defamed ministers Shanmugam and Tan See Leng.
The ministers said the decision upholds the integrity of public office.

cards.headline: China ramps up credit support in overhaul of property market
bullets: China is letting homebuyers take out mortgages for up to 40 years, longer than before.
The country is also helping developers raise money by selling shares and bonds.
New home prices in China continued to drop in July.
China wants developers to sell finished homes instead of pre-selling them.

cards.headline: Luxury watches, jewellery, bags: Highlights from the S$3 billion money laundering auction
bullets: A 15.02-carat diamond ring is expected to fetch up to S$300,000 at auction.
Luxury items seized in Singapore's S$3 billion money laundering case will be auctioned from late 2026.
Rare watches, jewellery, and handbags from the case will go under the hammer.
A Louis Vuitton pumpkin bag designed with Yayoi Kusama is among the items.
A Bulgari emerald and diamond necklace is also up for sale.

cards.headline: S$3b money laundering case: 15-carat diamond, Yayoi Kusama, Chanel items up for auction
bullets: A 15-carat yellow diamond and a rare Louis Vuitton bag from the S$3 billion money laundering case go on auction Sep 7.
Over 80 properties and more than 1,000 luxury items are being sold off in stages until mid-2027.
The first auctions include 338 handbags and 286 jewellery pieces, with estimates from a few hundred dollars to S$300,000.
High-end watches from Patek Philippe and Richard Mille, plus Hermes bags, will be sold in later auctions.

cards.headline: S$3b money laundering auction: How Hotlotz landed its biggest consignment
bullets: Hotlotz will auction luxury items seized in the S$3 billion money laundering case.
The local auction house secured the deal after a long selection process.
They will hold 15 online auctions over nine months.
The first sales feature handbags and jewellery worth millions.
Hotlotz moved online before Covid-19, which boosted their business.

cards.headline: Chinese robots have beaten Usain Bolt’s 100 m record. Should we be impressed?
bullets: A Chinese robot ran 100m in 8.86 seconds, beating Usain Bolt's record.
The robot crashed into a wall and caught fire after its record run.
Experts question if robot sports skills translate to useful real-world tasks.
Robot companies are getting investment and stock market attention.
Robots showing off athletic skills are still prone to falling and breaking.

cards.headline: Personal safety education, enhanced monitoring of informal gatherings with minors among new measures by MUIS to keep mosques safe
bullets: MUIS is introducing new safety rules for mosques after a recent abuse case.
Mosque staff will watch informal gatherings with children more closely.
Youth will get more education on spotting and reporting bad behaviour.
New rules will cover all mosques on how to keep people safe.
Mosques will also have checks on physical safety like lighting and cameras.

cards.headline: ICA raids: S'porean man, 59 & woman, 52, a Chinese national, arrested for suspected marriage of convenience offence
bullets: Immigration officers arrested a 59-year-old Singaporean man and a 52-year-old Chinese woman.
They are suspected of faking a marriage for immigration purposes.
The couple married in January 2025 but did not live together.
The man allegedly sponsored the woman's visit pass by claiming she lived with him.

cards.headline: Who's Firdaus Daud? The tech lawyer shadowing DPM Gan Kim Yong at Punggol now deployed to serve Kembangan residents.
bullets: Tech lawyer Firdaus Daud will now serve Kembangan residents.
He was previously seen with Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong in Punggol.
Firdaus will be the second grassroots adviser for Kembangan from September 1.
He will focus on Kembangan after previously serving in Punggol.
He also has experience advising small businesses and working with youth.

cards.headline: MapleSEA Has A New Mentorship System, Lucid Transformation & 21st Anniversary Event IRL
bullets: MapleSEA is celebrating its 21st anniversary with new events and a mentorship system.
The new Mentorship System lets experienced players guide newer ones to earn rewards.
Players can transform into the boss Lucid and complete missions for special items.
There's also an event set in the Omega Sector area, featuring the Mesorangers.
MapleSEA will hold a special IRL event in October for its 21st anniversary.

cards.headline: How To Get Up To $3 Cashback On PayLah! Every Week From Heartland Shops, Kopitiams & Wet Markets
bullets: Get up to $3 cashback weekly when you pay with DBS PayLah! at heartland shops.
The promo runs every Saturday from 6am until December 19, 2026.
You need to be a DBS PayLah! user and pay with the app to get the cashback.
Look for the red 'Scan to pay with DBS PayLah!' sticker at participating shops.
The cashback is limited to the first 160,000 redemptions each Saturday.
